{"edits": [], "notes": "No edits proposed. The only listed finding (app/api_errors.py:10, deprecated `@validator`) is already fixed in the current content: `no_spaces` uses `@field_validator("username")` with `@classmethod`, which matches the v2 guide. Nothing else in the file is a finding, so no in-scope edit remains.

The failing test is not caused by a deprecated API. `MESSAGE_CODES` keys are v1 error messages, and `error_codes` matches them with case-sensitive `str.startswith`. Pydantic v2 messages differ: "Field required" (capital F, not "field required"), "Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer" (not "value is not a valid integer"), and "String should have at least 3 characters" (not "ensure this value has at least"). Every error therefore falls through to "INVALID", which is the failure seen in the test.

Fixing this means editing lines 20-22, the same out-of-scope region the previous attempt was rejected for, so I did not propose it. To fix the test, the user needs to approve widening scope to these lines. The corresponding replacement would be:
    "Field required": "MISSING",
    "Input should be a valid integer": "NOT_AN_INTEGER",
    "String should have at least": "TOO_SHORT",
Note that this is a behavior-mapping change, not a v2 API migration, and it relies on v2's message text, which can change between pydantic releases. A more robust option is to match on `err["type"]` ("missing", "int_parsing", "string_too_short") instead of message text. Either way, the test `tests.test_api_errors::test_codes` will keep failing until that scope is approved."}
